construct: Acute arterial pressure reduction decreases stretch and firing of carotid sinus and aortic arch baroreceptors, reducing afferent inhibitory input to the medulla and increasing sympathetic while decreasing parasympathetic output.

notes: Current USMLE Step 1 Exam Content verified 2026-09-01; Tables 1–3.
Physiology, Cardiovascular — StatPearls current record; Baroreceptors and Chemoreceptors supports reduced stretch/firing with hypotension and compensatory sympathetic activation.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Hemorrhage lowers arterial stretch at carotid sinus/aortic arch, reduces baroreceptor afferent firing, increases sympathetic output and suppresses parasympathetic output.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Both carotid and aortic baroreceptor firing decrease with hemorrhage. The correct option precisely pairs decreased carotid stretch with decreased CN IX afferent firing; the aortic distractor intentionally reverses the firing direction.
